newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: INSIGHT-AUSSIE DLR OFF LOWS, BUT NOT OUT OF DANGER.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-AUSSIE DLR OFF LOWS, BUT NOT OUT OF DANGER.

text.p: The Australian dollar found enough support to push half a cent above two year lows established last week, but the amount of effort expended for the half cent rally suggested it was not out of danger yet.

Support at US$0.7300, just above the lows of US$0.7295 reached on Friday, had proved solid, but the lack of a solid bounce from that level left analysts feeling that the five month old downtrend from US$0.8000 still had some way to run.
By 8.00 a.m. the Australian dollar was at US$0.7352/57, up on its local close ot last week of US$0.7311/16.
After a number of attempts to rally, the dollar eventually made a break above US$0.7330, a move which triggered some short covering and took it to its overnight highs.
Switching out of the Canadian dollar also helped the unit, but analysts said a break above US$0.7410 resistance was really needed to show a change of sentiment on the dollar.
With the market still unsure about the direction of the next move in interest rates, the possibility of another rate cut remains a weight on the dollar and a reason to sell into any rallies.
The dollar reached its 1997 high of just above US$0.8000 in March, when the market was of the view that the easing cycle had come to an end.

Since then it has been in downtrend, with a run of softer data and two rate cuts in late May and July seeing the dollar establish a five month down-trend that has taken it to its lowest levels since July 1995.
While US$0.7300 was expected to provide some support, a break there would leave the way open for a move to US$0.7170, with any fall expected to pause at US$0.7250.
Traders will be looking to a speech by Reserve Bank Governor Ian Macfarlane on Tuesday night for clues to the rate outlook, in his first public speech in Australia since before the May 23 rate cut.
With a topic of monetary policy and growth, his comments will be examined closely for insights on the RBA's thinking.
Macfarlane will be in Perth, and as he is delivering a dinnertime speech, details of his speech will hit markets from 9.30 p.m. (1130 GMT), well after the local close.
